thread:
Carla (ACME): Hey team, we're seeing ~2s added latency on requests from ap-south1 since ~08:12 UTC. SDK is set to ap-south1. Request IDs: req-abc123, req-def456. Headers look normal but traces show backend in eu-west1. Can you take a look?

Kimberly (support): Sorry about that, Carla. Can you paste the request headers and a short traceroute? Also which SDK/version?

Carla (ACME): SDK v1.4.2. Header dump:

```
> POST /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.ai
X-Region-Pref: ap-south1
User-Agent: acme-sdk/1.4.2
X-Forwarded-For: 3.104.12.34
x-request-id: req-abc123
```

But our app logs say: `Routed-to: eu-west1` and p99 jumps to ~2.1s.

Raj (net): Can you run `traceroute -n api.redwood.ai` from the client and paste first 12 hops? Also `mtr -r -c 8 api.redwood.ai` if available. I want to see if traffic exits APAC to our eu transit.

Carla (ACME): Traceroute output below (from their VM in ap-south1):

```
traceroute to api.redwood.ai (52.17.45.180), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.128.0.1  0.6 ms 0.4 ms 0.7 ms
 2  100.64.0.1  1.2 ms 1.1 ms 1.3 ms
 3  203.205.12.1  5.6 ms 5.4 ms 5.7 ms
 4  13.32.24.10  18.9 ms 19.1 ms 19.0 ms
 5  52.95.76.2  53.2 ms 52.9 ms 53.0 ms
 6  15.197.6.34  118.3 ms 118.0 ms 118.5 ms
 7  52.17.45.180  118.8 ms 118.6 ms 118.9 ms
```

Kimberly (support): Hmm, hop 5->6 looks like an outbound handoff to a transit that lands in EU. Could be egress NAT overflow/overflow policy. @Raj can you check egress NAT pools for ap-south1?

Raj (net): Looking now. InfraBot, fetch egress-pool-metrics for ap-south1 last 30m.

InfraBot: Metrics job triggered: https://internal-metrics.redwood/egress/ap-south1?range=30m

Raj (net): I can see the ap-south1 NAT pool saturated at ~95% around 08:11-08:18 UTC. Overflow rule kicked in and traffic was rerouted to our eu-west1 egress cluster. Logs show `egress_pool=ap-south1 primary -> ap-south1-overflow -> eu-west1`. That explains the extra RTT.

Jules (oncall): Ok mitigation plan: 1) push a temporary customer-scoped routing override to prefer local region for ACME (5 min TTL), 2) increase ap-south1 NAT capacity and adjust autoscale thresholds, 3) follow up postmortem.

Kimberly (support): Raj, can you apply the override? Provide CLI snippet so I can notify the customer.

Raj (net): Applying now. CLI: 
```
redwood route update --customer acme --preferred-region ap-south1 --force --ttl 300
```
Applied at 08:25 UTC. Policy ID: pol-7782.

Kimberly (support): Carla, can you retry a few requests and report latencies? Also sending ACME a support ticket link.

Carla (ACME): Retried at 08:27 UTC — latency back to expected ~120ms p95. Header shows `Routed-to: ap-south1`. Thanks, that fixed it for now. Any idea on billing implications for rerouted traffic?

Raj (net): Overflow to eu-west1 could have added cross-region egress charges for those minutes. I'll add a cost estimate and include it in the ticket. Long-term fix: expand ap-south1 NAT pool and lower overflow threshold to 98% -> auto-scale earlier.

Jules (oncall): Filing follow-up action items: increase NAT pool cap, add alert when overflow rate > 0, run a chaos test for NAT saturation. Assigning to eng-infra for capacity changes.

Kimberly (support): Ticket created: TKT-3421. Assigned Raj + infra. Notifying ACME: we've applied temporary routing override and are working on permanent fix. :thumbsup:

Carla (ACME): Thanks everyone. Please keep me posted on timeline for the permanent fix and any billing adjustments.

Raj (net): Will follow up in TKT-3421 with metrics, ETA for NAT expansion, and cost estimate.

InfraBot: Auto-note: incident flagged as "egress-overflow". Severity: S2.

Kimberly (support): Closing thread here; will update ticket with notes and next steps.
